transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My wife wanted me to come in. What finally scared her is that I keep hearing water running, and men whispering inside the walls, but there’s nobody there. And sometimes I see this dark wet patch spreading across the hallway… but when I go check, it’s dry. It’s been really frightening.
How long have you been experiencing these sounds and visions?
About seven months now. It started after that winter freeze, when the house repairs turned into this huge mess I just couldn’t get out from under.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed over the past seven months?
Yes. Most days I wake up already feeling like I’ve failed—like I’m not being a good husband, not much of a man. It’s just this heavy feeling that sits on me all day until I go to bed.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually happy, energetic, or irritable?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get irritable sometimes, but not in a way where I feel unusually happy or full of energy. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt unusually happy or energetic for a few days or longer?
No, I don’t think I’ve had anything like that. I can’t remember a time where I was unusually happy or had extra energy for days.
Have you ever had a period where you weren't feeling sad or depressed, but instead felt extremely irritable for several days or longer?
No, I don’t think so. I get irritated sometimes, but I can’t think of a stretch of several days where I wasn’t depressed and was just extremely irritable instead.
Have you experienced any strange smells or tastes that aren't explained by anything around you?

Not really smells or tastes, no. It’s more like… I hear water running when there shouldn’t be any, and sometimes men whispering inside the walls. And I’ve seen what looks like a dark wet patch spreading in the hallway, but when I check it, it’s dry. That’s what scared my wife.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or have trouble keeping your thoughts straight?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I have trouble expressing myself most of the time. My thoughts can feel a little slow or foggy sometimes, but I wouldn’t say they’re all over the place.
Do you ever find yourself having trouble keeping track of what you're saying in conversations?
I don’t think so, not really. Sometimes I lose my train of thought for a second, but I can usually get back to what I was saying. I haven’t noticed it being a big problem in conversations.
Do you believe the men whispering inside the walls are actually there, or is it just something you hear?

It feels like they’re there when it happens. I know I check and nobody’s there, but I still hear the water running and men whispering in the walls. That’s what scared my wife, because I keep reacting to it even when there’s nothing there.
Do you think the men whispering in the walls are trying to communicate something to you or are they just random noises?

I don’t know that they’re trying to talk to me exactly. It’s more like I hear water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. And sometimes I’ll see this dark wet patch spreading across the hallway, even after I checked and it’s dry. That’s the part that really scared my wife.
Do you think the whispers and water sounds are real, or are they just something in your head?

I guess part of me knows it can’t be real, because I check and there’s nobody there, and the hallway is dry. But when it’s happening, it feels real. I hear the water running and the men whispering inside the walls, and sometimes I see that dark wet patch spreading even though I already checked. That’s what really scared my wife.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one topic to another when talking to someone?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can lose my place sometimes, but I haven’t noticed myself jumping from one topic to another a lot.
Do you often have trouble sticking to one topic when talking to someone?
Not really, no. I might pause or lose track a little, but I don’t think I have a big problem staying on one topic when I’m talking.
Are the sounds of water running and men whispering in the walls something you hear all the time, or do they come and go?

They come and go. It’s not every second, but it keeps happening—like I’ll hear water running, or men whispering in the walls, and then when I check there’s nobody there and it’s dry. Sometimes that dark wet patch looks like it’s spreading too, even after I already checked. That’s what really scared my wife.
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts organized when you're talking or thinking about something?
I’m not really sure. I can get stuck or lose my train of thought sometimes, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts are all over the place when I’m talking. It’s more like I slow down or have to pause.
Do you experience these whispers and water sounds in any other way, like feeling something or tasting something, besides just hearing them?

No, I don’t think I taste anything or feel anything from it. It’s mostly hearing the water running and the men whispering in the walls. And sometimes I see that dark wet patch in the hallway, like it’s spreading, even after I checked and it was dry.
Are the voices and sounds you hear something that happen at specific times of the day or can they occur at any moment?

It can happen at any time, as far as I can tell. I haven’t noticed a set time of day. I’ll just suddenly hear water running or men whispering in the walls, and there’s nobody there. Sometimes I check the hallway and it’s dry, but then I still see that dark wet patch like it’s spreading. That’s the part that really scared my wife.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed and had these hallucinations of hearing water running and men whispering in the walls at the same time?

Yes. The depression was there first, for at least a couple weeks, and then the hearing things started during that same stretch. Before all the house problems dragged on and I got so low, I wasn’t hearing men in the walls or seeing wet spots that weren’t really there. That only started after I’d already stopped caring about my normal life and was feeling like a failure every day.
